headline: Trincomalee & Pasikudah: Deep Harbour, Koneswaram Cliff & Coral Reefs
description:
When the south-west monsoon brings rain to the southern beaches, the east coast enjoys its best months: calm turquoise water, coral gardens off Pigeon Island and long, empty beaches from Nilaveli to Pasikudah.

Trincomalee’s deep natural harbour has drawn sailors for millennia, and the Koneswaram temple on Swami Rock is one of the most sacred Hindu shrines on the island — especially at sunset, when the devotional chants begin.

guideNote.heading: The Coast That Shines When the South Rains
paragraphs: For travellers coming between May and September I often swap the southern beaches for the east: the Cultural Triangle is only a few hours away, the sea is calm and the beaches are blissfully uncrowded.

experiences.title: Koneswaram Temple at Swami Rock
experiences.text: The “temple of a thousand pillars” on a cliff above the sea — evening devotional chants, the lovers’ leap viewpoint and, from March to April, the chance of whales below.

image.alt: Koneswaram Temple on Swami Rock above Trincomalee bay

experiences.title: Pigeon Island Private Snorkelling
experiences.text: A private boat to the marine national park before the day trippers, with blacktip reef sharks, turtles and parrotfish over the coral gardens.

fieldNotes.title: Reef Etiquette
fieldNotes.text: Never stand on or touch the coral. I provide reef-safe sunscreen and well-fitting masks for every guest.

fieldNotes.title: Temple Dress
fieldNotes.text: At Hindu kovils men may be asked to remove shirts and everyone removes shoes. A sarong or wrap is useful.

fieldNotes.title: Plan by Season
fieldNotes.text: October to January brings the north-east monsoon here — then I point guests to the south and west coasts instead.
